title: Graph-enhanced vector search (hybrid graph+vector retrieval)
keyFindings: Graph-enhanced vector search is a mature, production-stable family of hybrid retrieval techniques (Microsoft GraphRAG, TigerVector, Neo4j hybrid search, GNN-RAG, GRAG) that fuses a knowledge-graph layer with dense vector retrieval to recover the relationship data and explainability that pure vector search lacks.

Zodiac's `hybrid` query mode (zodiac.md §4.3.1/§4.3.2) is already the suite's in-spec implementation of graph-enhanced vector search — pre-graphed data + vector-embedded items merged at query time. This is the primary home of the technique and is MUST/already-specified.

Astrographer's Provident reference graph (astrographer.md §4.2) is already a knowledge graph; graph-enhanced vector search over it (enriching vector results with reference→fact relationship context) directly addresses the source talk's 'vectors don't capture relationship data' and 'similarity != relevance' concerns, and is a natural, low-cost extension of the RAG surface (§4.3).

The technique is fully D2/D1-compliant: the graph layer is already local (Provident graphs, Zodiac pre-graphing) and the vector layer uses local Ollama embeddings; the expensive sub-techniques (dynamic graph query generation, community summaries) are the D2 cost risk and should stay PARKED.

D4 parity applies: graph-enhanced retrieval is a retrieval-mode change, not a security-configuration feature, so it must be exposed on both GUI and MCP (rag_query/rag_stream for Astrographer §4.5.1, zodiac_query for Zodiac §4.5).

Index consistency is the dominant pitfall: when a fact value changes (astrographer.md §4.2.3) or a Zodiac refresh crawl updates the graph (zodiac.md §4.2), the vector embeddings must be re-synced in the same pass, or graph-enhanced retrieval returns stale/contradictory results.
summary: Graph-enhanced vector search (hybrid graph+vector retrieval) fuses a knowledge-graph layer with dense vector retrieval to recover the relationship data and explainability that pure vector search lacks. Zodiac's hybrid query mode (zodiac.md §4.3.2) is already the suite's in-spec implementation (MUST); Astrographer's Provident reference graph (§4.2) makes graph-enhanced vector search a natural, low-cost extension of its RAG surface (§4.3). The technique is D2/D1-compliant and D4-parity-relevant; the expensive sub-techniques (dynamic graph query generation, community summaries) stay PARKED for local-first cost reasons.
